subject: english
learningObjective: Identify and say red, blue, and green with familiar objects.
prerequisites: Can point to a named object
hints: Look for the apple that matches Aliz's red card.
Green is the color of this leaf.
successCriteria: Selects two of three named colors
commonMistakes: Points correctly but does not speak

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Offer two choices and model the word.
Offer three choices and pause before modeling.

content: Aliz names one color at a time, shows a safe everyday object, then invites pointing and an optional spoken response. Touch remains a complete response path.

subject: english
learningObjective: Follow one-step English directions using safe body actions.
hints: Aliz waves slowly first.
Aliz points to her head.
successCriteria: Matches one body word to the action

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Demonstrate while speaking.
Speak first, then demonstrate only as a hint.

content: Use playful one-step directions with no timer. Praise participation; never penalize a child who prefers touch or movement to speech.

subject: english
learningObjective: Count one to five food items and answer with a short English phrase.
hints: Touch each fruit once as we count.
The last number tells how many.
successCriteria: Uses number plus food word once

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Count together with visible number cards.
Hide number cards and ask for the short phrase.

content: Count familiar foods using visible one-to-one pointing. Accept the number alone before gently expanding it to a two-word phrase.

subject: english
learningObjective: Match the initial sounds c, d, and f to familiar animal words.
prerequisites: Knows the animal pictures cat, dog, and fish
teacherPrompts: Listen: fish. What sound comes first?
hints: D-d-dog. Listen to the first sound.
Watch Aliz's mouth for /f/.
commonMistakes: Says the letter name instead of sound

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Contrast two animal sounds.
Choose among three and produce one sound.

content: Model natural initial sounds without requiring perfect pronunciation. Use only the approved animal cards and repeat slowly when asked.

subject: english
learningObjective: Build I see a... sentences with familiar everyday objects.
prerequisites: Names cup, spoon, book, and ball
teacherPrompts: Choose an object and make a sentence.
hints: Start with: I see a...
The object is something we read.
commonMistakes: Uses this instead of I see

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Provide the sentence frame aloud.
Ask for color plus object.

content: Move approved room props into view and build one concrete sentence at a time. Recast gently rather than labeling grammar as wrong.

subject: english
learningObjective: Identify family-role words in short fictional descriptions.
teacherPrompts: Listen: This is Mina's sister. Point to the sister.
hints: A sister is a girl in the story's family.
Listen again for the family word.
commonMistakes: Uses a real family member's name

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Use two fictional picture choices.
Use four choices and a full sentence.

content: Use a fictional picture family. Do not ask for names, household details, or information about the child's real family.

subject: english
learningObjective: Describe visible actions with a subject and present-progressive verb.
prerequisites: Names run, read, eat, and sleep
teacherPrompts: Show me reading, then say the sentence.
hints: Start with She is.
Look at the book for reading.
commonMistakes: Uses the base verb after is

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Keep the sentence frame visible.
Remove the frame and mix four actions.

content: Describe only the action visible on approved cards. Accept a correct action word, then model the complete sentence once.

subject: english
learningObjective: Distinguish short a, i, and o in simple consonant-vowel-consonant words.
teacherPrompts: Choose the word with short i.
hints: Stretch the middle sound, not the first sound.
Short i is the middle sound in fish.

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Contrast two vowel sounds.
Sort all three vowel sounds.

content: Use clear natural pronunciation and visual word cards. A child may replay each approved sound without losing progress.

subject: english
learningObjective: Find the main idea and one supporting detail in a short original passage.
teacherPrompts: Read the garden story with Aliz.
What is the passage mostly about?
hints: Think about what all four sentences share.
Find one event from the passage.
commonMistakes: Adds a fact not in the passage

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Offer two main-idea choices.
Ask for an answer in the child's own words.

content: Mali puts a seed in a small pot. She gives it water and places it near the window. Soon, green leaves appear. Mali keeps caring for her growing plant.

subject: english
learningObjective: Use two observable adjectives to describe familiar food.
prerequisites: Names common fruit and basic colors
teacherPrompts: Describe the apple with two words.
How are the banana and apple different?
Build a sentence with looks or feels.

accepted: The apple looks red and round

hints: Choose one color and one texture.
Start with: The apple looks...
commonMistakes: Uses a personal preference instead of an observation

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Provide an adjective bank.
Compare two foods in one sentence.

content: Use illustrated foods rather than requesting eating or allergy information. Keep descriptions to observable color, shape, and texture.

subject: english
learningObjective: Make a simple inference and support it with evidence from an original passage.
prerequisites: Identifies explicit details and main idea
teacherPrompts: What can you infer about Arun?
Could another answer fit the evidence?
hints: An inference combines a story clue with what you know.
Look at what Arun did before the curtain opened.

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Offer two plausible inferences and compare evidence.
Ask for a second possible inference.

content: Arun arrived early and practiced each line softly. Before the curtain opened, he checked the script one last time. During the performance, he knew every line and spoke clearly.

subject: english
learningObjective: Express a choice and support it with a clear because reason.
prerequisites: Answers familiar what and which questions
teacherPrompts: Would you read about the ocean or space? Why?
Ask Aliz about her fictional choice.

accepted: I would choose the ocean because it is interesting
I would choose space because I want to learn about planets

hints: Start with: I would choose... because...
Give a reason about what you want to learn.
successCriteria: Supports it with a relevant reason
commonMistakes: Shares identifying personal details as a reason

difficultyVariants.adaptation: Use a sentence frame for one turn.
Compare both choices before deciding.

content: Keep the conversation on fictional learning preferences. Aliz gives a brief character answer and never asks for a name, school, location, phone number, password, or private family information.
